name: DOVS Annual Conference Showcases Global Research in Vision Science

content.title: DOVS Annual Conference Showcases Global Research in Vision Science
content.summary: Experts explore innovations in eye care at DOVS research conference

media.alt: DOVS Annual Conference Showcases Global Research in Vision Science

content.text: The Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences (DOVS) brought together leading experts and researchers for its Annual Research Conference held on October 9, 2025. The event highlighted innovative studies and global collaborations aimed at improving eye health and advancing the frontiers of vision science.

The conference opened with a series of presentations by speakers from Pakistan and abroad. Dr. Saleema Kherani-Ali from University of Austin Tx, USA shared her work on "Efficacy of Subcutaneous and Intravenous Tocilizumab in Non-infectious Uveitis," offering valuable insights into the use of immunomodulatory therapies for complex inflammatory eye diseases. From the University of Alberta, Canada, Professor Edsel Ing presented his study on "The Recognizability of Cropped Unilateral Upper Face Photographs." His research explored the intersection of facial recognition and ophthalmology, sparking engaging discussions among participants.

Professor Muhammad Moin from King Edward Medical University, Lahore, spoke about the impact of screening and establishing Peek-powered optometry clinics (Triage) at the primary healthcare level. His findings highlighted how integrating technology-driven screening can significantly reduce the burden on secondary healthcare facilities, making quality eye care more accessible across Pakistan. Mr. Moiz Mansoor Lakhani from the University of Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, presented results from a global pharmacovigilance analysis on the association of Anti-VEGF therapy with reported ocular adverse events which contributed to a growing understanding of treatment safety and patient outcomes in retinal care.

Reflecting on the impact of research, Dr. Salim Virani (Vice Provost, Research) said, "His Late Highness Prince Karim Aga Khan IV always emphasized the importance of knowledge sharing to improve lives and strengthen communities. This conference embodies that vision, where science and service come together for impact." The event concluded with a poster presentation session, where faculty and students shared innovative projects spanning various aspects of ophthalmic research.
